_comment: One input brief for Claude to reconcile through the existing lane; not a replacement global prompt file; no dispatch.
THESE RIDE IN EVERY PROMPT. They are data, not documentation, so an
editor adding a thirteenth item cannot forget them: the renderer appends
`rules_clause` to every positive prompt and refuses to build a prompt
that does not carry it (imagegen.py: build_prompt / _selftest_rules).
WHY: every 1980s British advert, poster and packet is still in copyright
for decades yet, and trade mark was the ONLY claim Getty actually won in
[2025] EWHC 2863 (Ch). A model asked for `a British high street in 1989`
will happily paint a real brewery's livery on a pub. So we never ask for
one. In-world brands only, which is better content anyway - MICKEY'S is
a place in this game and a real brewery is not.
AND THIS IS THE ONE CLAUSE THAT STAYS IN THE POSITIVE PROMPT, 25 Aug.
Every other exclusion moved to `negatives` below. This one did not, and
the reason is measured rather than cautious: sd-cli only evaluates the
unconditional branch when cfg != 1.0 (see `negatives._comment`), and this
batch runs at cfg 1.0 because Z-Image-Turbo is distilled for it. A
negative prompt is therefore INERT here - so moving the anti-brand,
anti-real-person clause into it would have deleted the only instruction
the model actually receives on the subject. It is mirrored into the
negative as well, where it will start acting the day an item raises cfg.
The exclusion scan in imagegen.py exempts this clause BY NAME and prints
that it did, so the hole is a line of output rather than a silence.
content_rules.rules_clause: invented fictional shop name only, no real company names, no real brand logos, no trade marks, no real person, no recognisable faces, no celebrity likeness

_comment: One shared style block so twelve prompts do not drift into twelve looks.
The reference is game-design/reference/ (GTA V frames, Jafar's, internal
comparison only) read for what a lettered street does, not copied.
`no people, no cars` USED TO BE IN THE SUFFIX and rode into all twelve
positive prompts. It is now `deserted, empty street` - the same intent
said as a thing to draw rather than a thing to omit - and the omission
half moved to `negatives.default`. This DOES change the positive prompt
of every item, so the resume rule regenerates all twelve on the next run;
that is deliberate and it is why the run publishes whatever is already on
disk BEFORE it generates anything (imagegen.py: Publisher.publish_existing).
The images he picked out are in git before the first pixel is redrawn.
`by_kind` overrides the whole prefix and/or suffix for one kind. A wall
texture is not a photograph of a street and must not be asked for as one:
the word `photograph` is exactly what produced a coping, a corner and a
pavement in a frame that was supposed to be nothing but brick.
2 SEP, AND THE SAME SENTENCE AGAIN AT FORTY-FIVE TIMES THE SIZE. A
verifier opened all 45 images: 41 of 45 are SCENE PHOTOGRAPHS, an object
standing in a street with pavement, sky and buildings around it, and 4 of
45 are plates. The four plates are the four `wall` items, which are the
only ones that were NOT asked for as a `photograph ... deserted empty
street`. Four of four. So the wall prefix below is not a wall-only idea,
it is the framing clause, and the DEFAULT is now that clause: sign,
fascia, notice and poster inherit it, and a kind added tomorrow inherits
it too rather than being born asking for a street.
ONE WORD DIFFERS FROM THE PROVEN STRING and it is named here so nobody
has to diff for it: `the surface filling the frame edge to edge` reads
`the artwork filling the frame edge to edge` for the signage families,
because a sign plate is not a surface sample. Everything else is copied
character for character from the wall prefix that worked.
`framing_required` IS THE PART THAT CANNOT BE FORGOTTEN. imagegen.py's
build_prompt refuses to return a prompt whose PREFIX does not contain
it, by id, before the 6.7 GB download - so a new item written
with no framing clause is a printed line rather than another photograph
of a sign in a street. It is deliberately the substring the wall prefix,
the signage prefix and the interior prefix all share; changing it here
without changing all three prefixes stops the whole batch. It is read
in the PREFIX only, and no suffix repeats it: the first version of that
guard was checked against the whole composed prompt, the old 1 Sep
prefix was planted back to see it go red, and it stayed GREEN because a
suffix carried the same words. A guard that cannot tell the regression
from the fix is a ratchet, so the words live in exactly one slot.
AND THE INTERIOR KIND IS NOT A SHOPFRONT. All three interiors came back
as exteriors photographed from the street, one of them with a garbled
fascia reading PORIE SHUOP, because they inherited the street suffix.
They are cards that sit BEHIND a window, so the frame is the room seen
from inside it: a shopfront applied there would put a second window, a
pavement and a sky inside the building.
style.framing_required: filling the frame edge to edge
style.prefix: flat orthographic texture sheet, square-on to the surface, uniform even lighting, the artwork filling the frame edge to edge,
style.suffix: British port town, late 1980s, damp salt-weathered paintwork, soot and grime, sharp legible lettering, period-correct signwriting, uniform lighting across the whole frame, one single flat surface

_comment: THE NEGATIVE CHANNEL, added 25 Aug. Composed as default + by_kind[kind] +
item.negative and passed to sd-cli as --negative-prompt.
THE FLAG IS VERIFIED FROM THE SHIPPED BINARY, not from a doc example.
`sd-cli.exe` out of sd-master-97d2990-bin-win-vulkan-x64.zip (38,784,820
bytes, the size pinned in imagegen.py) has `--negative-prompt` in its
string table followed by its own help text, `the negative prompt
(default: "")`, in the same table as --prompt, --cfg-scale, --steps and
every other long flag this pipeline already passes successfully.
AND THE PART THAT MATTERS MORE THAN THE FLAG: A NEGATIVE PROMPT DOES
NOTHING AT cfg 1.0. stable-diffusion.cpp's `resolve_guidance` sets
`use_uncond` only when `img_cfg != txt_cfg`; for a model with no image
conditioning img_cfg is forced to 1.0, so `--cfg-scale 1.0` means the
unconditional branch is never evaluated and the negative prompt is never
encoded. Z-Image-Turbo is distilled for cfg 1.0 (the project's own doc
page uses 1.0 for Turbo and 5.0 for Base), which is why this batch runs
there. So: the channel exists, it is wired end to end, and on the twelve
shipped items it is RECORDED AND INERT - the manifest says so per image
and the run summary counts both populations. The fix that actually
removed the sign from the brick wall is the positive prompt no longer
naming one.
The two `probe_*` items at the bottom are the measurement that decides
whether cfg > 1 is usable on this distilled model: same prompt, same
seed, same size, cfg 1.0 against cfg 2.0. Nothing else in this file
raises cfg, because a number nobody has measured is not a setting.
A NEGATIVE PROMPT IS A LIST OF NOUNS, NOT A SENTENCE OF REFUSALS.
Writing `no people` in the negative asks for `no people` to be pushed
away, which is not the same as pushing `people` away. imagegen.py's
validator refuses a negative containing `no `/`without`, and its
rejecting case is exactly that.
2 SEP: the four signage kinds now carry the SCENE half of the wall list
(kerb, pavement, road, ground, sky, roofline, building corner, street
furniture) because they had the same fault and only the wall was armed
against it. What is deliberately NOT copied across is the wall list's
anti-lettering half - `sign, signboard, lettering, letters, words` - for
the obvious reason, and `border` is left out of the four signage lists
because a fine printed border is the artwork on a telephone panel, a WAY
OUT plate and a tide table. These lists are still INERT at cfg 1.0. The
clause that will actually move the pixels is the framing prefix in
`style`, and it is the one that has four images of evidence.
